checks.remediation:
If the volume is already prepared, unlock and mount it at /mnt/data, then run the command again.
Setting up here would leave files on this computer's own disk, where an examination can find them.
Prepare the volume where nothing reaches this disk: on an external drive prepared on another computer (recommended), or from a setup medium (a live system started from a USB stick).
Then unlock and mount it here, and run the program from it.
Read "Where setup happens" in the operator guide on another device: opening it here leaves traces such as ~/.lesshst.

checks.message:
The decoy kernel does not zero freed memory: pages the hidden session frees keep their contents in RAM until something reuses them.
Add init_on_free=1 to the decoy kernel command line, and power off after a session rather than leaving the machine running.
checks.name: memory-wipe

checks.message:
The kernel is not remapping DMA through an IOMMU (the command line turns it off or into passthrough, /sys lists no active IOMMU, or every IOMMU group is identity-mapped), so any DMA-capable device — Thunderbolt or USB4, built-in PCIe, an NVMe/M.2 or ExpressCard slot — can map and read all of system RAM over the bus.
NAILS cannot turn DMA protection on for you: it lives in firmware — enable VT-d or AMD-Vi and "Kernel DMA Protection" in BIOS/UEFI setup, and, if the kernel still does not remap DMA, add the IOMMU flag to the decoy kernel command line and reboot. Those are NVRAM and boot-configuration changes NAILS refuses to make on your behalf, the same boundary that stops it setting the TCG Memory Overwrite Request (MOR) bit. No IOMMU makes a machine left powered on and unlocked safe against seizure, because a DMA peripheral reads RAM straight off the bus without the CPU; power off (`sudo /opt/nails/nails emergency --poweroff`) before the machine leaves your control.
checks.name: dma-protection

checks.message: the host would suspend an active session: closing the lid suspends the host (HandleLidSwitch=suspend). A suspend leaves the hidden session resident in RAM behind the hidden session's own lock screen. Set the logind lid switch to lock (see docs/decoy-requirements.md), or set sleep_policy.mode = "block" or "teardown" in nails.toml.
checks.name: sleep-policy

checks.message: decoy keeps a persistent record of the hidden session: systemd-journald keeps a persistent journal on the decoy disk (/var/log/journal); set Storage=volatile under [Journal] in /etc/systemd/journald.conf or in a drop-in such as /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/50-volatile.conf (drop-ins override the main file); rsyslog is active and writes logs to the decoy disk.
checks.name: decoy-persistence
checks.remediation: Make the decoy amnesic (Storage=volatile for journald, set in journald.conf or a journald.conf.d/*.conf drop-in; no active syslog or audit daemon, such as rsyslog, syslog-ng, a syslogd or auditd), or pass --allow-persistent-decoy to allow the risk for this run. See docs/decoy-requirements.md.
